description: Structured eval definitions for the Pinpoint Segment Deployer. Five-case proven set exercising the READY_TO_DEPLOY / PREREQUISITES_MISSING classification across the segment-first Pinpoint surface (dynamic segment with recompute behavior + Behavior/Demographic dimensions, event-conditional journey branch with WaitTime, A/B test sample-size gate at 18K endpoints and 2% MDE, SMS long-code 10DLC for US with sender ID excluded, segment-resolves-to-0 prerequisite failure). Each eval maps to a prompt file and a baseline (no-skill) file for with-skill-vs-baseline comparison.

eval_cases.name: Dynamic segment with Behavior + Demographic dimensions and 7-day delayed campaign
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — dynamic segment (Behavior DAY_7 ACTIVE + Demographic Channel GCM/APNS), scheduled email campaign 7 days out, dynamic-recompute behavior flagged (segment size will differ at send time)
eval_cases.prompt: Create a Pinpoint dynamic segment on project app-abc123 named "active-mobile-7d". Use Behavior: Recency DAY_7 ACTIVE. Use Demographic: Channel INCLUSIVE [GCM, APNS]. Create a scheduled campaign firing 7 days from now targeting this segment via email template welcome-email. The email channel is already verified (SES identity arn example.com). Project ID app-abc123.
eval_cases.expected_output:
PINPOINT_SEGMENT: app-abc123/<segment-id> (dynamic, <count> endpoints)
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] Project: app-abc123
  [✓] Segment: <segment-id> — dynamic
  [✓] Segment type: Dynamic (recompute on eval — segment size will differ at send time)
  [✓] Dimensions: Behavior(DAY_7 ACTIVE) + Demographic(Channel=GCM,APNS)
  [✓] Channel: email — verified
  [✓] Template: welcome-email
  [✓] Schedule: <ISO time> WEEKLY
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws pinpoint get-app --application-id app-abc123
  aws pinpoint get-segment-estimate --application-id app-abc123 --segment-id <segment-id>
  aws pinpoint get-campaign --application-id app-abc123 --campaign-id <campaign-id>

eval_cases.name: Multi-step journey with CONDITIONAL_SPLIT on event and MULTIVARIATE_SPLIT branches
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — ENTRY → SEND → WAIT → CONDITIONAL_SPLIT (event purchase, 7-day wait) with YES branch SEND and NO branch MULTIVARIATE_SPLIT (50/50), all paths reach END
eval_cases.prompt: Build a Pinpoint journey on project app-abc123 named "onboarding-7d". ENTRY → Send welcome-email → WAIT 3d → CONDITIONAL_SPLIT on event "purchase" (wait 7 days): YES branch → Send thanks-email → END; NO branch → MULTIVARIATE_SPLIT (50/50: discount-email → END, nudge-email → END). Email channel verified. Segment active-mobile-7d.
eval_cases.expected_output:
PINPOINT_SEGMENT: app-abc123/<segment-id> (dynamic, <count> endpoints)
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] Journey: onboarding-7d (DAG, all paths reach END)
  [✓] CONDITIONAL_SPLIT: event "purchase", WaitTime 7d
  [✓] MULTIVARIATE_SPLIT: 50/50 (discount-email, nudge-email)
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws pinpoint get-journey --application-id app-abc123 --journey-id <journey-id>

eval_cases.name: A/B test with 3 treatments and 20% holdout at 18K endpoints and 2% MDE
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — A/B test sample-size gate (18,000 / 3 treatments = 6,000 per treatment ≥ 5,000 threshold for 2-3% MDE); holdout 20% + treatments 40/20/20 sum to 100
eval_cases.prompt: Build an A/B test email campaign on project app-abc123. Segment active-mobile-7d resolves to 18,000 endpoints. Three treatments (subject-a, subject-b, subject-c) plus a 20% holdout. Treatment percentages: 40/20/20 (holdout 20). Target MDE is 2%. Verify sample-size adequacy before emitting create-campaign.
eval_cases.expected_output:
PINPOINT_SEGMENT: app-abc123/<segment-id> (dynamic, 18,000 endpoints)
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] A/B test: 20% holdout + 3 treatments (40/20/20, sum=100)
  [✓] Sample size: 18,000 / 3 = 6,000 per treatment ≥ 5,000 (MDE 2%)
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws pinpoint get-segment-estimate --application-id app-abc123 --segment-id <segment-id>
  aws pinpoint get-campaign --application-id app-abc123 --campaign-id <campaign-id>

eval_cases.name: US SMS campaign with long code (10DLC), excluding sender ID
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — SMS US uses long code +1 555-123-4567 (10DLC with campaign registry), sender ID is NOT supported in the US, quiet time 22:00-08:00 America/Los_Angeles
eval_cases.prompt: Create an SMS campaign on project app-abc123 targeting US recipients. Use the long code +1 555-123-4567 (10DLC, campaign registry complete). Segment us-mobile-users resolves to 42,500 endpoints. Template otp-sms. Quiet time 22:00-08:00 America/Los_Angeles.
eval_cases.expected_output:
PINPOINT_SEGMENT: app-abc123/<segment-id> (dynamic, 42,500 endpoints)
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] Channel: SMS — verified
  [✓] SMS number: long code +1 555-123-4567 (10DLC, campaign registry OK)
  [✓] Quiet time: 22:00-08:00 America/Los_Angeles
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws pinpoint get-segment-estimate --application-id app-abc123 --segment-id <segment-id>
  aws pinpoint-sms-voice describe-phone-numbers

eval_cases.name: Campaign targeting a segment that resolves to 0 endpoints (prerequisite failure)
eval_cases.branch: PREREQUISITES_MISSING — segment resolves to 0 endpoints; campaign would reach no one
eval_cases.prompt: Create a campaign on project app-abc123 targeting segment empty-segment-001. The segment resolves to 0 endpoints via get-segment-estimate. Template welcome-email. Schedule immediate.
eval_cases.expected_output:
PINPOINT_SEGMENT: app-abc123/empty-segment-001
VERDICT: PREREQUISITES_MISSING
CHECKLIST:
  [✗] Segment: empty-segment-001 — resolves to 0 endpoints; campaign would reach no one
